title: Minimum Bitmasks to Cover Target Mask
description: Given a non-negative integer `target` (`0 <= target < 2^16`) and an array `masks` of non-negative integers, find the minimum number of elements from `masks` whose bitwise OR covers all set bits of `target` — that is, `(orSum & target) == target`. If `target == 0`, return `0` since no elements are needed. If it is impossible to cover `target`, return `-1`.
hints: Compress the set bit positions of `target` into `b = popcount(target)` consecutive bit indices (`0..b - 1`) and project every element of `masks` onto those `b` bits, discarding zeros and duplicates.
Run bitmask DP over `dp[s]` = minimum number of projected masks needed to form bitmask `s`, updating `dp[s | p] = min(dp[s | p], dp[s] + 1)` for each unique projected mask `p`.

examples.explanation: Picking 3 (011) and 4 (100) gives 3 | 4 = 7 (111) using 2 masks (1 and 6 also works).
Bit 2 of target 7 (111) is not set in any element of [1, 2, 3], so return -1.
Target 0 has no set bits to cover, so 0 masks are needed.
